def: The number a search tries to improve, used as a stand-in for how close a candidate is to what you actually want.
A problem where following improvements in the objective leads away from the best solution.
A candidate that is better than all of its neighbours but worse than the best candidate overall.
A small deceptive test problem whose score rises toward a poor optimum and hides a single better optimum at the far end.
A search that selects candidates by how different their behaviour is from others seen so far, rather than by the objective.
A designer-chosen description of what a candidate does, used to measure how different two candidates are.
A growing memory of behaviours that were novel when first found, so the search does not revisit them.
An intermediate discovery that is valuable for what it leads to, even though it may score poorly on the final objective.
A website where people evolve images by choosing the ones they find interesting, used to study how discoveries arise without a fixed goal.
Novelty search that only accepts candidates meeting a basic standard of viability.
Letting each candidate compete on fitness only against candidates with similar behaviour, so many different kinds of good solution survive.
